topic: Brunswick whole-home renovation — WA Construct YouTube montage (v3 revision)
research_summary: This is a REVISION run, not a fresh concept exploration. An approved v2 render (22.17s, 1920x1080, 30fps, music-only) already exists and was supplied as the reference. Research was therefore conducted as a source-media review — a frame-by-frame teardown of v2 plus a full audit of the 25 graded stills in the client's Google Drive 'Edited' folder — rather than as web landscape research. DEVIATION NOTED: the cinematic manifest's research success_criteria asks for >=8 web searches; that criterion is not meaningful for a revision of an approved piece with a fixed, client-supplied asset pool, so it was not met. Findings below are grounded in the actual media.

existing_content.title: Brunswick_WA_Construct_YouTube_v2.mp4
existing_content.angle: Still-led Ken Burns montage with a gold-hairline lower third, closing on a white contact slate
existing_content.what_it_covers: 22.17s at 1920x1080/30fps over a music-only bed (-13.5 dB mean, -0.4 dB peak). Seven photo beats at roughly 2.5s each, then a ~4s end card. Beats: BRUNSWICK RENOVATION (bath vanity) 0.0-2.2 / A HOME TAKING SHAPE (bath sink) 2.2-4.8 / DESIGNED AROUND DETAIL (vanity light) 4.8-7.3 / PRECISION IN THE FINISH (tub + window) 7.3-10.2 / MATERIALS WITH INTENTION (teal marble shower) 10.2-12.8 / CRAFTED FOR DAILY LIVING (empty coral room) 12.8-15.3 / THE TRANSFORMATION CONTINUES (lived-in living room) 15.3-18.2.
existing_content.what_it_misses: Five of seven photo beats are the primary bathroom, so a whole-home renovation reads as a bathroom remodel. The closing living-room frame is a lived-in shot containing a child's tricycle, coffee-table clutter and a trailing cord. The end card is a plain white contact slate carrying no proof of the firm's track record.

existing_content.title: v2 lower-third treatment
existing_content.angle: Static bottom-left headline with a gold hairline rule and a 'WA CONSTRUCT' kicker beneath
existing_content.what_it_covers: Identical placement, weight and animation on all seven photo beats; white headline, gold kicker, thin gold rule spanning most of the frame width.
existing_content.what_it_misses: No escalation across the runtime — beat seven is typeset exactly like beat one, so the edit never builds.

existing_content.title: v2 end card
existing_content.what_it_covers: WA Construct logo lockup, gold hairline rule, 'LIVING INSPIRED.', 'BRUNSWICK', 'BOOK A CONSULTATION', 'WACONSTRUCT.COM | 201-485-8887'.
existing_content.what_it_misses: The white field breaks hard from the warm, dark grade of the seven beats before it; a large dead gap sits between the logo and the rule; and no verified credential (23+ years, SAM Awards, Best of Houzz) appears anywhere.

saturated_angles: Bathroom-only coverage: 5 of v2's 7 photo beats are the primary bathroom. The piece reads as a bathroom remodel reel, not a whole-home renovation.
Static centred lower third repeated identically on all seven beats — no visual escalation across the runtime.
Generic white 'contact us' end card — the most common end-card treatment in the contractor/renovation category and the weakest part of v2.
underserved_gaps: Three clean, finished living-room frames exist in the Drive folder and none were used; v2 instead used a lived-in shot containing a child's red tricycle, clutter on the coffee table and a trailing power cord.
A fully staged primary bedroom (dark green accent wall, upholstered bed, symmetrical lamps) exists in the folder and was never used — it is the strongest 'finished home' frame in the whole set.
Two finished powder-room frames (round mirror, vessel sink, black floating vanity) exist and were never used.
The landscape 'finished-primary-bathroom-*' set (1536x1024) is a better 16:9 fit than the portrait 'east_brunswick_*' bath crops (1632x2176) that v2 leaned on.
The end card carries no proof: no years in business, no awards, despite verified credentials being available.

data_points.claim: v2 duration is 22.166667s at 1920x1080, 30fps, with a stereo 44.1kHz AAC music bed; mean volume -13.5 dB, peak -0.4 dB.
The Drive 'Edited' folder holds exactly 25 graded PNG stills; 8 landscape 2304x1536, 8 landscape 1536x1024, 9 east_brunswick frames of which 6 are portrait 1632x2176.
v2's 'THE TRANSFORMATION CONTINUES' frame contains a child's red tricycle at frame right, objects scattered on the coffee table, and a black cord running across the floor.
WA Construct verified credentials: 23+ years in business; 2026 SAM Awards in Best Custom Home, Best Kitchen Remodeling and Best Building Renovation; 4x Best of Houzz.
WA Construct does not market standalone bathroom remodeling — bathrooms appear only inside larger scopes.

common_questions: Is this firm capable of a whole-home scope or just one room?
What does the finished work actually look like, not the construction process?
Are they established enough to trust with a large renovation?

misconceptions.myth: A montage weighted to one room still reads as a whole-home renovation because the title says so.
misconceptions.reality: Viewers read the pictures, not the title card. Five of seven bathroom beats makes a design-build firm look like a single-trade bathroom contractor — which also cuts against WA Construct's rule of never marketing standalone bathroom work.

misconceptions.myth: A lived-in room proves the home is finished and occupied, which is reassuring.
misconceptions.reality: Occupant belongings — a child's tricycle, objects on the coffee table, a cord across the floor — read as a real-estate listing photo rather than a builder's finished portfolio, and pull the eye away from the work itself.

angles_discovered.name: Whole-home walkthrough
angles_discovered.hook: Move room to room — bath, bedroom, powder room, living room — so the scope reads as a whole house.
angles_discovered.why_now: Corrects v2's bathroom-heavy weighting and aligns with the brand rule against standalone bathroom marketing.

angles_discovered.name: Finished-home close
angles_discovered.hook: End on staged, finished, uncluttered rooms so the last impression is a home someone lives in beautifully.
angles_discovered.why_now: The unused staged-bedroom and clean living-room frames make this possible without new photography.

angles_discovered.name: Earned end card
angles_discovered.hook: Replace the white contact slate with a dark, on-palette close that carries verified proof (23+ years, SAM Awards, Best of Houzz) alongside the CTA.
angles_discovered.why_now: The outro is the one element the client explicitly asked to redesign, and verified credentials are available but unused.

visual_references.description: v2 reference render — gold-hairline lower third over a warm cinematic grade
visual_references.what_works: The lower third is restrained, legible over busy interiors, and already reads as the series look — worth preserving for continuity even while the outro changes.

visual_references.description: Staged primary bedroom, dark green accent wall, upholstered bed, symmetrical lamps
visual_references.what_works: The only frame in the set showing a fully styled, lived-in-but-immaculate room; the deep green wall also sits closer to the brand's dark-and-gold register than the coral rooms do.

visual_references.description: Living room shot clean from the media-wall side, rug squared, nothing on the floor
visual_references.what_works: Same room and same warm floor as v2's rejected frame, so it slots in with no grade mismatch — but with no tricycle, no clutter and no trailing cord.

visual_references.description: Freestanding tub against the window in landscape orientation
visual_references.what_works: Native 3:2 framing means a gentle push-in instead of the hard portrait crop v2 needed, so the window light and the marble veining both stay in frame.
